glance: The EU has pushed its vote on Tesla's supervised driving system back to 15 December, and Europe's truck makers have cut their 2030 zero-emission forecast by more than half. In AI, SAP is reported to be weighing at least 10,000 job cuts tied to its AI push, and Reuters says US chip rules are slowing Chinese frontier models. BMW, Xiaomi, JTEKT, DeepL and ElevenLabs fill out the rest.
brief: Good morning. The European Union has moved its vote on Tesla Assisted Driving, the European name for supervised Full Self-Driving, from the first to the fifteenth of December. A rejection would also cancel the approvals that about a dozen countries have already given. Europe's truck makers now expect only about thirty percent of new heavy trucks to be zero-emission in 2030, down from sixty-eight percent in their forecast two years ago, although the ICCT still expects electric trucks to be cheaper to run than diesel by then. In AI, Bloomberg reports that SAP is weighing at least ten thousand job cuts as part of an AI-driven restructuring. SAP has not confirmed this. Reuters says US chip rules and defences against model copying are delaying Chinese frontier models from Zhipu and Moonshot. Zhipu calls the report fake news. In other news, BMW will send a twenty-four-feature software update to about sixteen million cars in December. Spain's Auto Plus electric car subsidy has run out of money for private buyers and will not be extended. Xiaomi is testing cars in Arjeplog and at the Nürburgring ahead of its 2027 European launch, while its car losses grow. JTEKT has launched a share buyback worth about nineteen billion yen, and Toyota will sell it ten million shares. DeepL launched Aure version two, a speech-to-speech translation model. Canada added seven hundred million Canadian dollars to its AI compute fund. ElevenLabs is reported to be in talks at a thirty-three billion dollar valuation. Volvo's electric A40 haulers have started work on London's Lower Thames Crossing.

stories.headline: EU delays its vote on Tesla's supervised driving system to 15 December
stories.why: The decision sets the precedent for how Level 2 systems that existing EU rules don't fully cover get approved across Europe.
body: The EU's Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) has moved its next meeting from 1 December to 15 December, the Commission confirmed to Reuters. Member states could vote there on EU-wide approval of Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD), which is what Tesla has called FSD (Supervised) in Europe since October, after Germany's transport minister criticised the old name.

The process rests on a provisional type approval that the Dutch authority RDW granted in April under Article 39 of Regulation 2018/858. Article 39 lets an authority approve new technology that the current rules do not yet fully cover. About a dozen member states, most recently Italy, have accepted it nationally. EU-wide approval needs a qualified majority: 15 of the 27 states, together representing at least 65% of the EU population. Reuters reports that a rejection would also cancel the national approvals.

For OEMs and suppliers developing hands-off and city driving assistants, the vote is a test of whether the Article 39 route can become a way to approve software-heavy ADAS features faster than UNECE regulations are updated.

stories.headline: European truck makers cut their 2030 zero-emission forecast from 68% to about 30%
stories.why: Volvo, Scania, Daimler Truck and their suppliers are planning around a much slower electrification of heavy trucks.
body: In the industry's latest survey, manufacturers expect about 30% of new heavy trucks over 12 tonnes sold in Europe to be zero-emission in 2030. In the 2024 survey the figure was 68%. For Germany, the forecast share of battery-electric trucks in 2030 has fallen to 24.2%, down from 48.2%.

The ICCT is more upbeat. It says that after the CO2 targets were eased, makers need about 39,000 electric trucks in 2030 to comply, down from about 90,000. That works out at roughly 14% of sales, against just over 5% today. Europe now has about 4,300 public charging points suitable for trucks, around 20% more than a year ago. The ICCT expects electric trucks to have a lower total cost of ownership than diesel in almost every European country by 2030, without subsidies. China, by contrast, sold about 400,000 electric trucks and buses in 2025, a 26% share.
For drivetrain and bearing engineers, a slower ramp means diesel and electric heavy-truck platforms will be built side by side for longer, which affects how test and validation budgets are split.

stories.headline: SAP is reported to be weighing at least 10,000 job cuts in an AI-driven restructuring
stories.why: Europe's largest software company is signalling that AI agents will change how many people build and sell enterprise software.
body: Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the plans, reports that SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 roles, more than 9% of its workforce. The scope could still change. Product, engineering and sales would be hit hardest, and other departments have been asked to find savings. SAP has not confirmed the figure. It said only that it reviews its organisation continuously.

SAP's employment guarantee with its German works council runs to 2028, so most of the cuts would probably fall outside Germany. The reported plan follows SAP's push into agents, including the Joule Work interface and Joule Assistants with more than 200 subagents, and comments from the CFO last week that headcount should fall. SAP usually announces restructurings in January. Its 2024 programme affected about 10,000 roles and cost about 3 billion euros.

For product teams that build on SAP or compete with it, the report suggests vendors expect agents to take over much of the configuration, support and implementation work that people do today. This is a report based on anonymous sources.

stories.headline: Reuters says US chip rules are delaying Chinese frontier models, and Zhipu denies it
stories.why: Release dates for the strongest open-weight models depend more and more on access to compute.
body: Reuters, citing two sources, reports that Z.ai (Zhipu) missed its planned November release of GLM-5.5, a model of about 3 trillion parameters, which could now slip to the first quarter of 2027 or later. Z.ai shipped GLM-5.4 on Monday instead, built on a 750-billion-parameter base. Moonshot's usual six-month release cycle could stretch to a year or more, which would push Kimi K4 to around mid-2027. Reuters adds that Moonshot began distilling from Google and Meta models after it became harder to get outputs from Anthropic and OpenAI.

The background is a US Commerce rule, in force since 19 November, that requires licences for overseas data centres running more than about 750 H100-equivalent chips. Existing operators have 90 days to comply. A Zhipu executive called the reports fake news on WeChat the same day, but did not give a date for GLM-5.5.
Teams that use Chinese open-weight models in their products, often for cost reasons, should plan for longer gaps between major releases. The story is contested.

stories.headline: BMW will push a 24-feature over-the-air update to about 16 million cars in December
stories.why: It shows how far a large OEM's software-defined fleet now reaches, including cars on older operating systems.
body: BMW's software version 11/2026.3 goes to about 16 million vehicles in 88 countries from December. It has five new functions and 19 improved ones. Cars on BMW Operating System X get all 24. Cars on OS 8.5 and OS 9 get nine. Installation takes about 20 minutes.

In Germany, Highway Assistant now works on more roads that have physically separated lanes. In the US, the Highway & Commuting Assistant now works in city traffic too: it can stop at red lights and pull away on green. Other additions include better forecasts of how busy public chargers will be, Google Maps Places data in destination search, a driving-style analysis for the iX3, and a more capable AI voice assistant in France and Spain.

Shipping ADAS changes over the air to a fleet this size depends on regression testing and simulation-based sign-off across many hardware and software combinations, which is the kind of virtual validation workload many OEMs are now scaling up.

stories.headline: Spain's Auto+ EV subsidy runs out for private buyers and will not be extended
stories.why: Another European EV incentive ends early, which makes demand harder to forecast for 2027.
body: Spain's Auto+ purchase subsidy for electric cars ran out of money for private buyers on 19 November. A waiting list now covers applications that are withdrawn or rejected. The 2026 budget was about 400 million euros: 350 million for private buyers and 50 million for businesses and the self-employed.

By mid-November, about 103,000 applications averaging 3,167 euros had used 93% of the private budget, and 86% of the business budget had gone. An Industry Ministry official ruled out an extension, citing legal and budget limits and the coming parliamentary elections. Auto+ started in July, applied back to 1 January, and replaced the regionally run Moves III scheme.

Spain is a major production country for Stellantis, Renault and Volkswagen Group. An early end to the incentive could weaken local EV demand going into 2027, just as automakers work toward the EU's averaged CO2 targets.

stories.headline: Xiaomi tests cars in Arjeplog ahead of its 2027 EU launch as its car losses grow
stories.why: Another Chinese EV maker is coming to Europe and validating its cars at Swedish winter test sites.
body: Xiaomi is testing its cars at seven sites in Sweden, Germany, Spain and Italy ahead of a European launch, including the Arjeplog winter test area and the Nürburgring. Germany will be its first market. Xiaomi has letters of intent with eight German dealer groups, including Emil Frey, and plans to exhibit at IAA Mobility in September 2027. Cars built in China face a 45.3% EU countervailing duty.

The car division's third quarter was weaker. Its operating loss rose to 3.4 billion yuan, from 2.6 billion in the second quarter. Deliveries fell 7.2% to 100,975, and gross margin dropped to 19.2% from 25.5%. Xiaomi has delivered about 336,000 cars in ten months, against a full-year target of 550,000.
Arjeplog's test service providers and engineering consultancies get another Chinese client, and European OEMs get a competitor whose cars are built around its own software stack.

stories.headline: JTEKT launches a 19 billion yen share buyback, and Toyota will sell it 10 million shares
stories.why: Toyota is loosening its hold on one of the world's largest bearing and steering suppliers, but remains its biggest shareholder.
body: JTEKT, which makes Koyo bearings and steering systems, has started a tender offer to buy back up to 11,000,100 of its own shares, 3.45% of the total, for up to about 19 billion yen. The price is 1,733 yen a share, about 9% below the 25 November close of 1,898.50 yen. The offer runs from 26 November to 23 December.

Toyota Motor has said it will tender 10 million shares, 3.14% of JTEKT, and is expected to remain the largest shareholder. JTEKT plans to cancel 9.5 million of the shares it buys back on 15 February 2027. If more shares are offered than planned, purchases will be scaled back pro rata.

It is part of a wider unwinding of cross-shareholdings in Japan's car supply chain. For European buyers of Koyo hub, tapered roller and e-axle bearings, the Toyota relationship itself does not change, but JTEKT is under more pressure to raise returns on capital.

stories.headline: DeepL launches Aure v2, a speech-to-speech translation model, and reports fast growth in voice use
stories.why: Live voice translation is quickly becoming a standard feature in meeting and service products.
body: DeepL launched Aure v2 at its first Unmute Summit in Tokyo, just 15 days after the first version. Aure translates speech directly into speech, without a text step in between. DeepL says the median delay is half what it was. In its own benchmark of one-minute real recordings across ten language pairs, DeepL reports 32% fewer English–Japanese errors than Google's Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, while noting that real-world results may differ.

Aure v2 launches in English, German, French, Spanish, Japanese and Korean. It is available in DeepL Voice for meetings, DeepL Voice for in-person conversations, and the Voice API. DeepL says voice minutes grew more than eightfold year on year in the third quarter, and active meeting subscriptions grew about ninefold in Germany.
For product teams, an API with this latency makes live multilingual support, field service calls and supplier meetings realistic features to build. The benchmark figures are DeepL's own.

stories.headline: Canada adds 700 million Canadian dollars to its AI Compute Access Fund
stories.why: Governments are starting to pay for domestic AI compute directly, as Europe debates doing the same.
body: Canada has added 700 million Canadian dollars to its AI Compute Access Fund, bringing it to 1 billion. In the first phase, more than 52 million dollars went to 45 companies, and total commitments now exceed 118 million dollars across 89 Canadian firms.

The next phase is organised by sector, starting with an open call for health and life sciences, and coverage says it favours domestic cloud providers. The fund supports the federal budget's pledge of 500 megawatts of sovereign AI compute. The government estimates that AI adoption could add up to 200 billion dollars to the economy by 2034.

For European readers, the model is close to what EU AI Factories and national schemes offer: subsidised compute tied to local providers. That matters to engineering firms that need GPUs for simulation surrogates or model training but cannot send data to US hyperscalers.

stories.headline: ElevenLabs is reported to be in early talks to raise money at a 33 billion dollar valuation
stories.why: Investors are still paying high prices for AI voice companies whose revenue is growing fast.
body: Bloomberg reports that ElevenLabs is in early talks to raise money at a 33 billion dollar valuation, up from 22 billion in its last round. The company is aiming to close in the first quarter of 2027, and the deal may include a sale of existing shares. The size of the round is not known. Annualised revenue is reported at about 700 million dollars, up 100 million since September.

ElevenLabs recently released its Eleven v4 and v4 Turbo voice models, the latter with 150-millisecond latency, and bought Japan's Kotoba earlier this month. Its chief executive has said IPO preparations will start in 2028. The company has not confirmed the talks.

Read together with DeepL's launch, the funding shows voice becoming a main way to use software, not an add-on. Product teams adding voice agents have more capable vendors to choose from, and those vendors have strong pricing power.

stories.headline: Volvo CE's A40 Electric haulers start their first job, on London's Lower Thames Crossing
stories.why: A Swedish-built heavy electric machine is now in real use, with a known battery size and charging time.
body: Four Volvo A40 Electric articulated haulers, built in Braås, Sweden, are working on the UK's Lower Thames Crossing for BMJV, a joint venture of Bouygues TP and J Murphy & Sons. It is the model's first deployment anywhere. The machines move material at the tunnel entrance and for road foundations.

Each hauler carries 39 tonnes, has a 540 kWh battery and runs about six hours on a charge. On a 350 kW charger it goes from 10% to 90% in about an hour. The site's chargers run on generators fuelled by British-made green hydrogen, and the project says it has used no diesel since 2025.

For drivetrain engineers, high-payload electric haulers put heavy demands on e-motor bearings, gearboxes and thermal management. Data from real sites like this one will feed back into duty-cycle models and test programmes.

watch.title: SKF Vertevo listing
watch.text: SKF's automotive bearings business starts trading on Nasdaq Stockholm on 1 December. The record date is today. Index changes at the 1 December close could bring forced selling.

watch.title: Guangzhou motor show
watch.text: The show opens today and runs to 6 December, with 1,106 vehicles, 64% of them new-energy, and 115 debuts, including the next BYD Han and an 800-volt Leapmotor.

watch.title: Tesla TAD vote
watch.text: Watch how EU member states line up before the 15 December TCMV meeting. A qualified majority is needed for EU-wide approval.
